CS 690U Project 2025¶

Diverse Genome Embedding Benchmark¶

Declaration of Intent: \

Basic Idea: Compare a simple model with a complex model from the DGEB paper in case of EC-Classification -> do we really need a complex foundation model?

Using AA (amino acids)

I will test or plot: \

The performance (e.g., F1-score) of a logistic regression model trained on one-hot encoded protein sequences for EC number prediction. I will also compare this performance to published results from foundation models in the DGEB benchmark.

If the hypothesis is true, I will observe: \

The logistic regression model will achieve comparable performance (in terms of F1-score) to the foundation model baseline on the EC Classification task, indicating that simple models can be effective with basic encodings.

If the hypothesis is false, I will observe:

The logistic regression model will perform significantly worse than the foundation models, suggesting that the complex, pre-trained representations are capturing important functional features that simple models miss.

Idea:¶

Getting TSV -> Do One-Hot-Encoding -> Split -> train Modell -> test Model -> comapare Results with DGEB -> discussion¶

UniProt Dataset¶

In [ ]:
tsv_file = "uniprotkb_ec_AND_reviewed_true_AND_frag_2025_04_10.tsv"  
df = pd.read_csv(tsv_file, sep='\t')

# Just keep the relevant columns with exact one EC number
df = df[df['EC number'].notna()]
df = df[df['EC number'].apply(lambda x: ";" not in str(x))]
# print(df)

#  just keep classes with at least 5 sequences
df['EC_class'] = df['EC number']
class_counts = df['EC_class'].value_counts()
print(f"Anzahl:",class_counts)
valid_classes = class_counts[class_counts >= 5].index
df = df[df['EC_class'].isin(valid_classes)]

# Fit sequence length
max_len = 256 #512  
aa_list = list("ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY")
def clean_sequence(seq):
    seq = seq[:max_len]
    seq = ''.join([aa if aa in aa_list else 'X' for aa in seq])
    return seq.ljust(max_len, 'X')
df["CleanedSeq"] = df["Sequence"].apply(clean_sequence)

Hot-Encoding¶

In [4]:
# One-Hot-Encoding
def one_hot_encode_sequence(seq):
    matrix = np.zeros((max_len, 21))
    for i, aa in enumerate(seq):
        idx = aa_list.index(aa) if aa in aa_list else 20
        matrix[i, idx] = 1
    return matrix.flatten()

X = np.stack(df["CleanedSeq"].apply(one_hot_encode_sequence))
y = df["EC_class"].values

print("Dataset successfully computed.")
print("Input shape:", X.shape)
print("Number of classes:", len(set(y)))

DGEB Dataset¶

Load Dataset from Huggingface¶

In [15]:
from datasets import load_dataset

dataset = load_dataset("tattabio/ec_classification")
train_data = dataset["train"]
test_data = dataset["test"]

Hot-Endcoding¶

In [ ]:
# define acid_list
aa_list = list("ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY")
max_len = 256 #512  

def clean_and_encode(seq):
    seq = seq[:max_len]
    seq = ''.join([aa if aa in aa_list else 'X' for aa in seq])
    seq = seq.ljust(max_len, 'X')
    one_hot = np.zeros((max_len, 21))
    for i, aa in enumerate(seq):
        idx = aa_list.index(aa) if aa in aa_list else 20
        one_hot[i, idx] = 1
    return one_hot.flatten()

Prepare Dataset¶

y_test = [x['Label'] for x in test_data]

print("Testdaten:", X_test.shape, y_test[:5])

# Result-Plot: F1-Score und Accuracy

Train logistic regression models with different values of reularization strenght (C)¶

Train model with different C values¶

In [12]:
# Define values for C (inverse of regularization strength)
C_values = [0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100]
accuracy_scores = []
f1_scores = []

for C in C_values:
    model = LogisticRegression(
        solver='saga',
        multi_class='multinomial',
        max_iter=300,
        C=C,
        penalty='l2',
        verbose=0
    )
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
    
    acc = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)
    f1 = f1_score(y_test, y_pred, average='weighted')
    
    accuracy_scores.append(acc)
    f1_scores.append(f1)
    print(f"C = {C:<6} → Accuracy = {acc:.4f}, F1-Score = {f1:.4f}")

from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer

# Prepare sequences as strings
sequences = [x['Sequence'] for x in train_data]  # from your huggingface dataset

# Define k
k = 3  # 3-mer 

# Create k-mer tokens from sequence
def seq_to_kmers(seq, k):
    return ' '.join([seq[i:i+k] for i in range(len(seq)-k+1)])

kmers = [seq_to_kmers(seq, k) for seq in sequences]

# Count frequency of each k-mer
vectorizer = CountVectorizer()
X_train = vectorizer.fit_transform(kmers)

print("Shape of Feature Matrix:", X_train.shape)

Shape of Feature Matrix: (512, 7986)

sequences_test = [x['Sequence'] for x in test_data]
kmers_test = [seq_to_kmers(seq, k) for seq in sequences_test]
X_test = vectorizer.transform(kmers_test)

In [ ]:
# Result-Plot: F1-Score und Accuracy
f1 = f1_score(y_test, y_pred, average='weighted')
acc = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)

plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
plt.bar(['F1-Score', 'Accuracy'], [f1, acc], color=['skyblue', 'lightgreen'])
plt.ylim(0,1)
plt.title('Model Performance')
plt.ylabel('Score')
plt.show()

print("F1-Score:", f1)
print("Accuracy:", acc)
 

F1-Score: 0.15130208333333334
Accuracy: 0.1953125

k-mer method increases the result from F1-socre of 0.057 and accuracy of 8.5%. to F1-score 0.1513 and accuracy = 19.53%

Define embedding function (mean pooling)¶

In [5]:
def get_esm2_embedding(sequence):
    inputs = tokenizer(sequence, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True)
    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs = model(**inputs)
    # Average pooling over token embeddings
    embedding = outputs.last_hidden_state.mean(dim=1)
    return embedding[0].numpy()

Apply to training & test sequences¶

DGEB Data Set¶

In [6]:
# Convert huggingface datasets to lists
train_sequences = [x["Sequence"] for x in train_data]
train_labels = [x["Label"] for x in train_data]

test_sequences = [x["Sequence"] for x in test_data]
test_labels = [x["Label"] for x in test_data]

# Generate embeddings
X_train_embed = np.stack([get_esm2_embedding(seq) for seq in train_sequences])
X_test_embed = np.stack([get_esm2_embedding(seq) for seq in test_sequences])

Asking to truncate to max_length but no maximum length is provided and the model has no predefined maximum length. Default to no truncation.

Evaluate Predictions¶

In [ ]:
# Evaluate Predictions
accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test_customDS, y_pred_customDS)
f1 = f1_score(y_test_customDS, y_pred_customDS, average='weighted')  # weighted = considers class imbalance

print("Accuracy:", accuracy * 100, "%")
print("F1-Score:", f1)

print("\nDetailed classification report:")
print(classification_report(y_test_customDS, y_pred_customDS))

# Visualize confusion matrix
ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_estimator(model_customDS, X_test_customDS, y_test_customDS)
plt.xticks(rotation=90)
plt.show()
